The gate-pass-rate probe (enumerate at bound 4, decide at Base and ZTime, evaluate the eight gates per invalid verdict) did not finish in 25 minutes and was stopped. evalBranchGates re-runs buildTableau for every invalid verdict, roughly doubling DECIDE cost; the per-cell gate pass rate is unmeasured and is the first figure the plan's opening phase should take.

Two copies of the gate-pass-rate probe ran concurrently for ~20 minutes. The first launch call failed on its PID-file write (an unquoted scratchpad variable resolved to /yield.pid, Permission denied) but had ALREADY backgrounded the lean job, so the relaunch added a second elaboration competing for the same cores; and killing the recorded PID only killed the subshell, leaving the timeout/lake/lean children alive. Both instances were found via pgrep and killed. Lesson: quote the scratchpad path variable, and kill the process GROUP or the timeout wrapper's own PID, not the subshell's.

Research report's compiled probe had already elaborated the full five-declaration L-level substitution construction AND run register_theorem on a generalized row, so the plan's critical-path phase is authored against a verified shape rather than a hypothesis.

Phase 1 probe's gate_ms column is contaminated and must not be read as the marginal cost of gating. The per-gate histogram accumulates Nat fields inside a List.foldl (h.timeOrderTotal + b g.timeOrderTotal), which Lean builds as a thunk chain; the IO.monoMsNow window around the fold therefore measures thunk construction only, and every Base row reported 0 ms while the real tableau rebuild cost is paid when the row is printed. The gate PASS-RATE figures (per-gate counts and GATED) are unaffected and valid, since printing forces them. The marginal-cost figure needs a separate measurement that forces the accumulator before stopping the clock.

CORRECTION to the earlier gate_ms issue entry for this dispatch: the lazy-accumulation diagnosis was wrong and is withdrawn. The DECIDE stage uses the identical List.foldl-over-a-Nat-structure shape and reported a nonzero 35 ms / 38252 ms, so the fold is strict and the timed window does capture the tableau rebuilds. gate_ms=0 at Base is therefore a REAL measurement, not an artifact. The actual finding is that gating cost is wildly asymmetric across frame classes: negligible at Base, and so expensive at Dense that four ModalBoolean gate rows did not finish in nine minutes of wall clock. That asymmetry, not a timing bug, is the Phase 6 input.

The plan's Phase 1 mitigation for timing contamination -- take the measurement once under the shared .lake/build-guard.lock -- is INSUFFICIENT, and this dispatch measured why. That lock serializes lake invocations only. The actual contention source during this run was a sibling dispatch's 'run-all.sh --jobs auto' shell test sweep over ~120 suites (pid 2935696) plus several concurrent claude processes, none of which take the lake lock: load average 6.45 on 24 cores. ModalBoolean's DECIDE stage took 38s on the first run and had not finished after 5.5 minutes on the second, identical run. CONSEQUENCE: under a multi-task /orchestrate batch, no wall-clock figure from this probe may be presented as uncontended. The COUNT figures (per-gate histograms, four-way decision splits, enumeration yields) are contention-independent and reproduced exactly across both runs, so they stand.

The plan's per-phase 'Files to modify' lists omit the TEST LIBRARY ROOTS (Tests/BimodalLibTest.lean, Tests/BimodalToolsTest.lean) while listing the individual test files under them. A new test file is not in the build at all until its root imports it, so the omission is load-bearing. Phase 2's five-declaration L-level uniform substitution (substF, substF_reflectTime, Axiom.ofSubst with 20 arms, Axiom.minFrameClass_ofSubst, DerivationTree.subst with 7 arms, DerivationTree.substNil) compiled clean on the FIRST build with no warnings, because FormalSystem/PlusLanguage/Substitution.lean is an arm-for-arm template at the L-plus level and the plan said to mirror it. #print axioms gives [propext, Quot.sound] for substNil -- no sorryAx, no Classical.choice -- which is exactly what register_theorem accepts. Mirroring an existing verified module beat deriving the proof structure from scratch by a wide margin.

Phase 7's task 'add assert_no_subsumed_entries to BimodalLib/Theorems/Complete.lean, so non-redundancy of the registry becomes a build invariant' cannot be executed as written. The command, landed in Phase 3, reports 26 of the 190 live registry rows as substitution instances of another row, and they are deliberate named laws rather than defects: Combinators.topThm's own proof term is literally 'identity Formula.bot', so it IS Combinators.identity at bot, and Propositional.em unfolds to (A -> bot) -> (A -> bot), an instance of A -> A. Wiring the unscoped command globally would turn the build red on 26 hand-curated entries the reference manual cites. Per .claude/rules/plan-compliance.md this was RAISED rather than silently substituted: the command was landed with assert_registry_complete's own optional prefix argument (the plan told Phase 3 to mirror that elaborator), the unscoped form is implemented and available, and nothing is wired globally, so the build is green under any ruling. user_decision set on .return-meta.json with three options; the scoped form over BimodalLib.Theorems.Enumerated is the recommended default. Phases 4-6 do not need the ruling.

Lean.Json.mkObj stores fields in a search tree, so a rendered record is ALPHABETICAL, not in the order its toJson source list builds. Any 'field order is Head.keys ++ Stage.reservedKeys s' claim is therefore about the pre-render association list only. Phase 5's five records each expose toJsonFields/toJson/keys so the order assertion reads the list; the golden strings are alphabetical.

Lean block comments NEST, so one opening delimiter inside a generated doc comment opens an inner comment that the doc comment's own closing delimiter then closes, leaving the outer unterminated. Symptom: 'unterminated comment' at END OF FILE, pointing nowhere near the cause. Trigger here: the recorded reproduce-command carried a scratch path beginning with a slash and a hyphen. Fixed by BimodalTools.commentSafe plus a path-free reconstructed invocation in the generated module; the sanitizer's own docstring and its tests must not spell the delimiters out either, which cost two further build failures to learn.

Check C23 forbids an outer-shadows-inner bare-declaration pair anywhere in the live tree, because C17's dead-declaration census keys on the last dot-segment and two declarations sharing a base name mask each other. A new 'writeJsonl' in BimodalTools.TheoremLibraryPipelineMain collided with the existing BimodalTools.writeJsonl (ProofFirstGenerator.lean:75); renamed to writeJsonObjects. Any new declaration under a BimodalTools.* submodule must have a base name unique across the whole library.

A ModalBoolean complexity-4 run at a 2-atom pool went end to end in under 7 minutes: 40 decided (valid 3, invalid 29, fuelExhausted 5, extractionFailed 3), 3 admitted, 0 subsumed, 25 conjectures, 12 gated_tableau refutations, 141 records across all five stages. The generated module elaborated sorry-free with register_theorem accepting all three entries at [propext, Quot.sound], max line 98. That discharges Phase 7's dominant risk (kernel cost of the generated module) in advance, and confirms extractionFailed is a principal path at a bound below the one it was measured at.

The driver's two bounds do not cover CERTIFY. --timeout-ms bounds decideOne only; the tableau rebuilds that follow it (rebuildOpenBranch plus evalBranchGates at Base, Dense and RTime) are pure, untimed computations, and --deadline-s is checked only at the TOP of each formula's loop iteration. So one formula can exceed the whole-run budget indefinitely. Measured: an --all-fragments run with --deadline-s 9600 stalled at checkpoint serial 3954 (inside ModalTemporalBoolean) for over ten minutes with no advance, which is Phase 1's recorded Dense-over-a-modal-fragment cost wall. Compounding it, records are written only after the loop, so killing a stalled run loses every record. Remedy used: re-run at --deadline-s 2400, the configuration measured to complete. Follow-up: give CERTIFY its own IO.asTask budget and flush records incrementally.

The plan's ADMIT step specified self-subsumption among candidates only, which under-implements the task's own ADMISSION rule ('unless it is a substitution instance of an entry already present'). Two separate defects followed. (1) A single accumulating fold is order-dependent: a less general candidate seen first is admitted and the more general one arriving later is not an instance of it, so both are kept -- 2 of 10 entries. (2) Nothing compared against the hand-curated registry -- a further 2 of 10 duplicated FormalSystem.Theorems.ConnectDerived.lceImpThm. assert_no_subsumed_entries caught all four, which is the prefix-scoped invariant earning its place on its first real run. Fixed with a two-pass ADMIT plus a registry snapshot (specs/evidence/theorem-library-pipeline/registry-statements.lean, --registry-statements): 6 admitted, 7 subsumed.

simpa closes the generalized entry's goal but routes an arity-2 entry through Classical.choice, which the plan's own validation criteria forbid on a registry row. Measured: the nine entries of arity 0 or 1 reported [propext, Quot.sound] under simpa while the one arity-2 entry reported [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]; the nested ite chain of a two-atom substitution drags it in. Remedy: simp only [substF, <subst>, reduceIte] at h then exact h, which cannot reach a classical lemma because the lemma list is closed. The closer must be arity-aware -- at arity 0 there is no ite and naming either argument is an unusedSimpArgs warning, hence a --wfail failure.

The ruled-bound run reproduced its figures identically across four successive invocations (3955 decided, 24927 records, 2981 refutations, 2895 conjectures), and the admitted yield landed inside the plan's Scope Hypothesis: 6 non-subsumed schemata against a predicted 'eight to ten' before registry filtering removed four. ZTime contributed 0 of 2981 refutations, exactly as Decision 12 predicted structurally. BimodalLib builds clean with all three build-time assertions green.
